qAndA.question: What is the purpose of the rheostat in the experiment?

qAndA.answer: To ensure that the electromotive force (e.m.f.) of the battery remains constant throughout the experiment, leading to more accurate results.

An orange banner with the text 'Procedure'
A circuit diagram illustrating the conversion of a galvanometer into a voltmeter.
Text A. Conversion of the galvanometer into voltmeter:'
A numbered list explaining the steps of conversion
The circuit diagram shows a galvanometer labeled as 'G', connected in series with a resistance labeled 'R'.
The diagram also shows the whole setup connected to a potential difference, 'V', across its terminals
The list item '1. Note down the given value of galvanometer resistance G and its figure of merit K.'
The list item '2. Note the total number of divisions (n) on either side of the zero of the galvanometer.'
The list item '3. Calculate the value of current, Ig with the help of the relation Ig = nK for which galvanometer shows full scale deflection.'

The list item '4. Calculate the value of required series resistance R to be connected in series with the galvanometer for the conversion of the given galvanometer into voltmeter of given range by the relation R = V/Ig - G.'
The list item '5. Connect a resistance box of range 0 to 10,000 ohm in series with the given galvanometer and take out the plugs of resistance R from it.'
Text 'Now the given galvanometer with this resistance in series is converted into voltmeter of the given range V volt.'
The circuit diagram now shows a battery with the '+' and '-' terminals, a one-way key 'K', and a rheostat connected in series.
The resistance box and the converted voltmeter with resistance R and galvanometer G are connected in parallel to this series combination.

props.name: An orange banner with the text 'Observations'
The list item '1. Given resistance of the galvanometer (G) = x ohm
The list item '2. Given value of the figure of merit of the galvanometer (K) = A/division.
The list item '3. Total number of divisions on either side of the zero of the galvanometer (n) = x divisions.
The list item '4. Current for full scale deflection (Ig) = nK = x amp.
The list item '5. Range of conversion of the converted voltmeter (V) = x ohm.
The list item '6. Value of the required series resistance (R) = V/Ig - G = x ohm.
The list item '7. Least count of the converted voltmeter V/n = x volt.
The list item '8. Least count of the standard voltmeter = x volt.
Table for the verification of converted voltmeter.
An orange banner with the text 'Result'
The list item '1. The value of the required series resistance to be connected in series with the galvanometer to convert it into voltmeter of the given range = x ohm.
The list item '2. Value of the current for full scale deflection, Ig = x amp.'

The list item '3. The difference between the values of standard voltmeter and converted voltmeter, i.e. (V2 - V1) is very small, hence, conversion of the given galvanometer into voltmeter of the given range is perfect.'

narrativeProgression.description: The scene highlights precautions to be taken during the experiment and potential sources of error, including battery EMF changes, calibration errors, loose plugs, and unequal galvanometer divisions.

props.name: An orange banner with the text 'Precautions'
The list item '1. All the connections should be neat, clean and tight.'
The list item '2. The resistance box to be used in series should have a very high resistance as compared to resistance of galvanometer and that to be used in parallel should have a low resistance.'
The list item '3. A freshly charged battery should be used so that its e.m.f. may remain constant throughout the experiment.'
The list item '4. All plugs in the resistance box should be tight.'
The list item '5. The deflection in galvanometer should be large.'
The list item '6. The rheostat should be used as a potential divider.'
The list item '7. The voltmeter used for verification should preferably be of the same order, as the range of conversion.'
An orange banner with the text 'Sources of Error'
The list item '1. The e.m.f. of the battery may change during the experiment.'
The list item '2. Calibration of resistance in resistance box may not be correct.'
The list item '3. Plugs in resistance box may not be tight and may have contact resistance.'
The list item '4. The galvanometer divisions may not be of equal size.'

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: To convert the given galvanometer of known resistance and figure of merit into a
voltmeter of a desired range and verify the same. Galvanometer is a sense
that a device used to detect very low current. Its working is based on the
principle that a coil placed in a uniform magnetic field experiences a torque
when an electric current is set up in it. Madam, how can we convert the given
galvanometer of known resistance and figure of merit into a voltmeter of a
desired range and verify the same? A galvanometer can be converted into a voltmeter
of desired range by connecting a suitable high resistance R in its series. Let
G be the resistance of the galvanometer which gives full-scale deflection when
I G current flows through it. Let V is the range of the voltmeter in which the
galvanometer has to be converted and R is the resistance required to connect in
series with the galvanometer. Then resistance R is given by R is equal to V by I G
minus G. Let's do an experiment to convert the given galvanometer of known
resistance and figure of merit into a voltmeter of a desired range and verify
the same. Our aim here is to convert the given galvanometer of known resistance
and figure of merit into a voltmeter of a desired range and verify the same.
A parameters required are a Western type galvanometer of known resistance and
figure of merit, a battery, a real start, one-way key, a resistance box of the
range 0 to 10,000 ohm, a voltmeter of 0 to 3 volt range connecting wires and
sandpaper. Procedure A conversion of the galvanometer into voltmeter, no
term the given value of galvanometer resistance G and its figure of merit, K. Note
the total number of divisions N on either side of the zero of the galvanometer.
Calculate the value of current I G with the help of the relation I G is equal to
N K for which galvanometer shows full-scale deflection. Calculate the value of
required series resistance R to be connected in series with the galvanometer for
the conversion of the given galvanometer into voltmeter of given range by the
relation R is equal to V by I G minus G. Connector resistance box of range 0 to
10,000 ohm in series with the given galvanometer and take out the plugs of
resistance R from it. Now the given galvanometer with this resistance in series is
converted into voltmeter of the given range V volt. B, verification of the
converted voltmeter, draw a neat circuit diagram for the verification of the
converted voltmeter. Remove insulation from the ends of the connecting wire
using a sandpaper. Arrange the apparatus according to the circuit diagram and
make all connections neat and tight. Take out the plugs of calculated resistance
R from the resistance box of the range 0 to 10,000 ohm and insert the key K and
adjust the real start to obtain maximum deflection in the galvanometer.
Note the readings of standard voltmeter and galvanometer. Can word the galvanometer
reading into volt and find the difference between them. If any, this difference
gives the error. Take four more observations by changing the resistance with the
help of the real start over the whole range of the voltmeter. Record all the
observations in a tabular form. Observation given resistance of the galvanometer
G is equal to X ohm. Given value of the figure of merit of the galvanometer K is
equal to A by division. Total number of divisions on either side of the zero of
the galvanometer N is equal to X divisions. Current for full scale deflection I G is
equal to N K is equal to X ampere. Range of conversion of the converted voltmeter
V is equal to X ohm. Value of the required series resistance R is equal to V by
I G minus G is equal to X ohm. Least count of the converted voltmeter V by N is
equal to X volt. Least count of the standard voltmeter is equal to X volt. Table
for the verification of converted voltmeter. Zero number. Reading of converted
voltmeter. Deflection theta division. Potential difference 3 1 is equal to
theta into LC. Volt. Standard voltmeter reading V2 volt. Difference error V2 minus V1. Volt.
Result. The value of the required series resistance to be connected in series with the galvanometer
to convert it into voltmeter of the given range is equal to X ohm. Value of the current
for full scale deflection I G is equal to X ampere. The difference between the values
of standard voltmeter and converted voltmeter that is V2 minus V1 is very small. Hence,
conversion of the given galvanometer into voltmeter of the given range is perfect. Precautions.
All the connections should be neat clean and tight. The resistance box to be used in series
should have a very high resistance as compared to resistance of galvanometer and that to be
used in parallel should have a low resistance. A freshly charged battery should be used so
that its EMF may remain constant throughout the experiment. All plugs in the resistance
box should be tight. The deflection in galvanometer should be large. The real start should be used
as a potential divider. The voltmeter used for verification should preferably be of the same
order as the range of conversion. Sources of error the EMF of the battery may change during
the experiment. Calibration of resistance in resistance box may not be correct. Plugs in
resistance box may not be tight and may have contact resistance. The galvanometer divisions
may not be of equal size. Thank you, ma'am, for this knowledgeable experiment.
